```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Report set-up: libraries, paths and the helpers used throughout"
#
# This report does NOT re-run the pipeline. The pipeline is a set of
# standalone scripts under code/analysis/ (several steps run on the Slurm
# cluster for hours, BLAST outputs reach 150 GB). The report reads what
# those scripts wrote under results/ and metadata/, and shows the full
# source of every script beside its results. Every number quoted in the text
# is computed from those files at render time, so the prose cannot drift
# from the outputs.
#
# Re-render after re-running any part of the pipeline:
#   /data/hb-austick/work/miniforge3/envs/tick_report/bin/quarto render report/tick_microbiome_report.qmd

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)   # all table handling
  library(knitr)        # kable() for small tables
  library(DT)           # searchable tables for anything long
  library(ape)          # mitogenome tree in section 17
  library(ggplot2)      # the palette figure in the software section
})

ROOT <- normalizePath("..")                       # project root (report/ is one below)
R    <- function(...) file.path(ROOT, ...)        # absolute path inside the project
REL  <- function(...) file.path("..", ...)        # relative path, for images

# read a TSV from the project; returns NULL (not an error) if a step hasn't run
rtsv <- function(...) {
  p <- R(...)
  if (!file.exists(p)) return(NULL)
  fread(p, na.strings = c("", "NA"))
}

# Small tables print as static markdown; long ones become searchable,
# sortable, paged widgets so the report stays readable.
tbl <- function(d, caption = NULL, page = 12, digits = 3) {
  if (is.null(d)) return(cat("*(table not produced: the step has not been run)*\n"))
  d <- as.data.frame(d)
  num <- vapply(d, is.double, logical(1))
  d[num] <- lapply(d[num], function(x) signif(x, digits + 1))
  if (nrow(d) <= page) return(kable(d, caption = caption))
  datatable(d, caption = caption, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
            extensions = "Buttons",
            options = list(pageLength = page, scrollX = TRUE, dom = "Bfrtip",
                           buttons = c("copy", "csv")))
}

# A pipeline figure; relative path so Quarto can embed it in the HTML
fig <- function(...) include_graphics(REL("results", "figures", ...))

# Show the complete source of a pipeline script in a collapsible block.
# Used with `results: asis`. Four backticks so the scripts' own text can't
# close the fence early.
show_code <- function(rel, open = FALSE, note = NULL) {
  p <- R(rel)
  if (!file.exists(p)) return(cat(sprintf("\n*`%s` not found*\n", rel)))
  x <- readLines(p, warn = FALSE)
  lang <- switch(tools::file_ext(p), py = "python", R = "r", sh = "bash",
                 yaml = "yaml", yml = "yaml", tsv = "default", "default")
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "\n<details class=\"pipeline-code\"%s><summary>&#128196; <code>%s</code> &nbsp;",
    "<span style=\"color:var(--bs-secondary-color)\">%d lines%s</span></summary>\n\n",
    "````{.%s .code-overflow-scroll}\n%s\n````\n\n</details>\n\n"),
    if (open) " open" else "", rel, length(x),
    if (is.null(note)) "" else paste0(" &middot; ", note),
    lang, paste(x, collapse = "\n")))
}

pct <- function(x, d = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), x)
n_  <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
params <- yaml::read_yaml(R("config", "analysis_params.yaml"))
excl   <- fread(R("metadata", "excluded_samples.tsv"), skip = "sample_id")
```

```{r}
#| label: headline-numbers
#| code-summary: "Headline numbers used in the overview"
audit  <- rtsv("results", "audit", "sample_completeness.tsv")
meta   <- rtsv("metadata", "sample_metadata.tsv")
# identification changes against the metadata of the previous run
old_meta <- rtsv("results", "_pre_exclusion_20261008", "metadata", "sample_metadata.tsv")
id_fix <- merge(old_meta[, .(sample_id, previous = tick_species)],
                meta[, .(sample_id, corrected = tick_species, notes)], by = "sample_id")[
  is.na(previous) != is.na(corrected) | (!is.na(previous) & previous != corrected)]
frac   <- rtsv("results", "tables", "fraction_summary.tsv")
tsum   <- rtsv("results", "targets", "target_summary.tsv")
n_all  <- nrow(audit)
# samples in the abundance matrix = its columns. (fraction_summary.tsv has one
# more row: a sample whose contigs all fail the evidence filter.)
mat_ids <- names(fread(R("results", "matrices", "tpm_microbial_genus.tsv"), nrows = 0))[-1]
n_mat  <- length(mat_ids)
n_xy   <- sum(meta$has_coords == "yes")
n_gen  <- uniqueN(na.omit(meta[sample_id %in% mat_ids]$tick_genus))
n_sp   <- uniqueN(meta[sample_id %in% mat_ids & species_identified == "yes"]$tick_species)
med_unassigned <- median(frac$tpm_pct_no_lca)
```

# Overview {#sec-overview}

This document is the complete record of the analysis of the microbial communities,
endosymbionts and pathogens in the Barker collection of Australian ticks. Each
tick was sequenced as a whole-tick shotgun metagenome, then assembled, and the
contigs were classified by BLAST plus a lowest-common-ancestor (LCA) call.

| | |
|---|---|
| samples catalogued | **`r n_all`** |
| samples with abundance data (analysed) | **`r n_mat`** |
| tick genera / identified species among analysed samples | **`r n_gen` / `r n_sp`** |
| samples with GPS coordinates | **`r n_xy`** |
| median share of each library with *no* BLAST hit | **`r pct(med_unassigned)`** of TPM |

**How to read this document.**

* Every step has the same shape: what it is for → the **decisions** taken (blue
  boxes) → the **full source code** (fold-out boxes marked &#128196;) → the
  **results** it produced → how to read them.
* Code that *this report* runs to draw tables is folded under "Show the code
  that produced this". Pipeline scripts are in the &#128196; boxes. Both are
  commented line by line, and the comments are part of the documentation.
* Long tables are searchable and sortable, and can be copied or saved as CSV
  with the buttons above them.
* Section numbers follow the pipeline. The pipeline's own step numbers (`00`,
  `04b`, `10b`…) are given in each heading.

## What changed in this version {#sec-changes}

This version re-runs every analysis after a review of the mitogenome results
(@sec-mito-audit):

* **`r nrow(excl)` samples were removed from every analysis** (microbiome,
  markers, trees, mitogenome). They are listed with reasons in
  `metadata/excluded_samples.tsv` and in @sec-audit. Most hold a different tick
  from the one recorded, or a mixture of two.
* **Tick identifications were corrected** in the curated metadata for
  `r nrow(id_fix)` samples, using the mitogenome and nuclear-rRNA evidence
  (@sec-metadata).
* **Step 21 now selects only tick mitogenome contigs.** A candidate contig must
  have a tick (Ixodida) nt-BLAST LCA, and ties are broken by coverage. Before
  this fix, blood-meal and bacterial contigs were chosen for 7 samples.
* **A new step 26c audits every genus-discordant sample.** It uses the sample's
  nuclear rRNA hits to decide between "contaminant mitogenome", "mixed tube"
  and "wrong tick".
* **Every figure now uses one style**: `theme_classic()` with light-grey major
  gridlines, and colour-blind-checked palettes built from the CSIRO brand
  colours (@sec-colours).

## Three things to know before reading any result {#sec-caveats}

::: {.callout-important}
## 1 · Most of every library is unidentifiable, by design of the reference database
A median of **`r pct(med_unassigned)`** of each sample's TPM sits on contigs
with no BLAST hit at all. Australian tick genomes are essentially absent from
`nt`, so the tick's own DNA, which is most of a whole-tick homogenate, gets no
hit. An independent read-level classifier (Kraken2) leaves the same bulk
unclassified. **No statement of the form "X % of this tick is microbial" is
supportable.** The analysis unit is therefore `tpm_microbial`: abundance
renormalised *within the microbial fraction*, which never uses the unassigned
bulk as a denominator.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## 2 · There are no negative controls
No extraction blanks or no-template controls were sequenced. Composition is
**descriptive**. Reagent-contaminant genera are **annotated, never removed**
(`metadata/reagent_contaminants.tsv`), and every figure carries this caveat.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## 3 · Abundance and evidence are different things
TPM is length-normalised, so a 400 bp contig with 6 reads can outrank a whole
genome. **A taxon is called *present* only when its read and contig evidence
clear fixed thresholds** (≥ `r params$taxon_filter$min_contigs_per_taxon`
contig and ≥ `r params$taxon_filter$min_reads_per_taxon` reads). Read counts
gate presence calls and are **never** used as an abundance.
:::

# Software, configuration and how to reproduce {#sec-env}

Three conda environments are used, each for a reason:

| env | used for | why separate |
|---|---|---|
| system `python3` (pandas, taxopy) | steps 00–05b, 10, 11–25 | no R needed |
| `tick_micro` (`env/tick_micro.yml`) | R steps 06–10b, 19b, 26, 26b | R 4.3 / Bioconductor 3.18 (mia 1.10), pinned |
| `tick_markers` (`env/tick_markers.yml`) | BLAST+, MAFFT, FastTree, IQ-TREE | bioinformatics binaries |
| `tick_report` (`env/tick_report.yml`) | maps (10c) and this report | sf / leaflet / Quarto, no Bioconductor |

::: {.decision}
**Maps and the report live in their own environment.** Adding the spatial
packages (`sf`, `leaflet`) to `tick_micro` made the solver upgrade the whole
environment: R 4.3 → 4.4, mia 1.10 → 1.14, ggplot2 3.5 → 4.0. That transaction
then failed on a Bioconductor data package and was rolled back. Rather than
silently change the version of every package the analysis was built on, the
analysis environment was left pinned. Maps and the report, which read only
TSV/PNG outputs, got their own small environment.
:::

**To reproduce everything after the cluster backfills:**

```bash
bash run_all.sh       # steps 0, 3-10c  (tables, TSE, figures, comparisons, maps)
bash run_markers.sh   # steps 11-16     (marker genes for each target)
bash run_trees.sh     # steps 17-19b    (marker-gene trees)
bash run_mito.sh      # steps 20-26     (tick mitogenome phylogeny, incl. 20b references)
Rscript code/analysis/26b_mito_vs_metadata.R
quarto render report/tick_microbiome_report.qmd
```

**All thresholds live in one file.** No script hard-codes a threshold, so the
configuration below *is* the methods section.

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
show_code("config/analysis_params.yaml", note = "every threshold used anywhere")
show_code("run_all.sh", note = "the main driver")
show_code("env/tick_micro.yml"); show_code("env/tick_report.yml")
```

## Figure style and colour {#sec-colours}

Every figure is drawn with `theme_classic()` plus light-grey major gridlines in
both directions (`theme_tick()` in `code/analysis/common.R`). All colours come
from the CSIRO palette in `CSIRO_colours.R`.

::: {.decision}
**The CSIRO colours were chosen and ordered by computation, not by eye.** Each
candidate set was simulated under protanopia and deuteranopia
(Machado–Oliveira–Fernandes 2009) and scored by colour difference (OKLab ΔE).
The nine hues below keep **every pair** at ΔE ≥ 8.7 under both deficiencies and
≥ 15.8 under normal vision, and the first *k* slots are the best-separated set
of *k*. That makes all nine safe to use together, even in a scatter plot where
any two colours can sit side by side. Steel grey was rejected for "other"
because it collapses onto Mint and Fuchsia under deuteranopia; Mist is used
instead.
:::

::: {.decision}
**Colour is never the only cue.** Several CSIRO hues are very light (Gold,
Light Mint) or very dark (Midnight Blue) and cannot be lightened or darkened
without leaving the brand palette. Every filled mark therefore has a dark
outline, and every figure also encodes identity by shape, facet or a direct
label. A categorical figure never shows more than nine colours: beyond that,
the rest fold into "other" (Mist). Magnitudes (heatmaps) use a single-hue
white → Midday Blue → Ocean Blue → Midnight Blue ramp, which reads correctly
under any colour-vision type.
:::

```{r}
#| label: palette-figure
#| code-summary: "Draw the palettes"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| fig-cap: "The palettes used in every figure. Top: the nine categorical CSIRO slots in their fixed order, with 'other'. Middle: the tick-genus colours. Bottom: the sequential ramp for magnitudes."
local({
  e <- new.env(); sys.source(R("CSIRO_colours.R"), envir = e)
  cs  <- unlist(mget(ls(e), envir = e))
  cat_names <- c("Blueberry", "Mint", "Gold", "MiddayBlue", "MidnightBlue", "Orange",
                 "LightMint", "Fuschia", "Plum", "Mist")
  genus <- c(Amblyomma = "Mint", Ixodes = "Blueberry", Haemaphysalis = "Orange",
             Bothriocroton = "Gold", Argas = "Fuschia", Ornithodoros = "Plum",
             Alectorobius = "MiddayBlue", Cryptocroton = "LightMint",
             Rhipicephalus = "MidnightBlue", unidentified = "Mist")
  ramp <- colorRampPalette(c("#FFFFFF", "#CCEEF5", cs[c("MiddayBlue", "OceanBlue", "MidnightBlue")]))(9)
  d <- rbind(
    data.table(row = "categorical slots", x = seq_along(cat_names),
               lab = sprintf("%s\n%s", c(seq_len(9), "other"), cat_names), col = cs[cat_names]),
    data.table(row = "tick genus", x = seq_along(genus), lab = names(genus), col = cs[genus]),
    data.table(row = "sequential", x = 1:9, lab = "", col = ramp))
  d[, row := factor(row, levels = c("categorical slots", "tick genus", "sequential"))]
  ggplot(d, aes(x, row)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = col), colour = cs[["MidnightBlue"]], linewidth = 0.3, width = 0.95, height = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(label = lab), size = 2.3, vjust = 2.6, lineheight = 0.85) +
    scale_fill_identity() + scale_y_discrete(limits = rev, expand = expansion(add = c(0.9, 0.5))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), axis.line = element_blank())
})
```

```{r}

#| echo: false

```

# Sample reconciliation — step 00 {#sec-audit}

**Why.** The upstream pipeline was run incrementally, and the artefact
directories (`contigs/`, `blast/`, `lca/`, `mapping/`, reads) disagreed about
which samples exist. Two samples even had different file names in different
directories. Step 00 builds the single authoritative inventory that every
later step reads, so nothing downstream has to guess.

::: {.decision}
**File-name aliases are resolved in a table, not by renaming files.**
`metadata/sample_aliases.tsv` maps `8334-AMLoculosum-BriddledTurn7` →
`8334-AMLoculosum-BriddledTurn` and `B6852_F1_38_1` → `B6852_F1_38_S1`.
The raw data stay untouched and the mapping is visible.
:::

::: {.decision}
**Every exclusion has a diagnosed reason** (`results/audit/excluded_samples.tsv`).
A sample is never silently missing from a figure.
:::

::: {.decision}
**Samples removed by decision are listed in one file, and the raw data are
untouched.** `metadata/excluded_samples.tsv` gives each removed sample and why.
Step 00 gives them the status `excluded_manual`, which every later step
honours. Step 21, which reads the assemblies directly, skips them as well. To
restore a sample, delete its row and re-run.
:::

```{r}
#| label: manual-exclusions
#| code-summary: "Samples removed from every analysis, and why"
tbl(merge(excl, meta[, .(sample_id, recorded_as = tick_species, host_species)],
          by = "sample_id", all.x = TRUE)[, .(sample_id, recorded_as, host_species, reason)],
    "Samples removed from every analysis (metadata/excluded_samples.tsv)")
```

```{r}
#| label: audit
#| code-summary: "Audit status counts and the excluded samples"
tbl(audit[, .N, by = status][order(-N)], "Samples by pipeline status")
tbl(rtsv("results", "audit", "excluded_samples.tsv"), "Excluded samples and why")
```

The *needs_lca* and *needs_mapping* queues that this audit wrote have since been
processed by steps 01–02 (@sec-backfill). That is why `r n_mat` samples now
reach the matrix.

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
show_code("code/analysis/00_audit_samples.py")
show_code("metadata/excluded_samples.tsv", note = "samples removed by decision")
show_code("code/analysis/common.py", note = "shared Python helpers: config, aliases, paths")
```

# Cluster backfills — steps 01, 02 and the streaming LCA {#sec-backfill}

**Why.** 12 samples had BLAST output but no LCA, and 24 had an LCA but were
never read-mapped.

* **LCA never ran because the original `code/lca.py` loads the whole BLAST
  table into memory.** Seven BLAST files are 10–150 GB, so it ran out of
  memory. `lca_stream.py` streams the file one query at a time. Its peak
  memory was measured at a flat 2.34 GB on the 149 GB file. The
  classification logic is unchanged.
* **NCBI has merged taxids since the local April 2026 taxonomy dump.**
  `merged.dmp` from the current dump rescues them; before, they silently
  became "unclassified". `make_merged_filtered.py` drops the ~2% of merge
  targets newer than the local dump, which would otherwise crash taxopy.

::: {.decision}
**The taxonomy dump (`nodes.dmp`, `names.dmp`) was *not* updated.** The 120
samples already classified were called against the April 2026 dump. Swapping
it would make backfilled samples incomparable with them.
:::

::: {.decision}
**The Slurm scripts are POSIX `sh`.** This cluster runs batch scripts with
`/bin/sh` whatever the shebang, so bash-only syntax fails at submit time. Queue
files hold paths relative to the project root, so they work under either mount
point.
:::

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
show_code("code/analysis/lca_stream.py", note = "constant-memory LCA")
show_code("code/analysis/make_merged_filtered.py")
show_code("code/analysis/01_backfill_lca.sh")
show_code("code/analysis/02_backfill_mapping.sh")
show_code("code/analysis/submit_backfills.sh")
```

# Taxonomy and scope — step 03 {#sec-taxonomy}

**What.** Every LCA taxid gets a full lineage and is put into one of five
**scopes**:

| scope | rule | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `host` | phylum Arthropoda | the tick itself |
| `bloodmeal` | phylum Chordata | vertebrate DNA from the blood meal |
| `microbial` | Bacteria, Archaea, Viruses, and Eukaryota *outside* Metazoa/Viridiplantae | the analysis target |
| `other_eukaryote` | other Metazoa / plants | e.g. nematodes, pollen |
| `ambiguous` | LCA above domain (`root`, `cellular organisms`) | genuinely unresolvable, not forced into a class |

::: {.decision}
**The scope rules were checked against the local taxonomy, not assumed.** NCBI's
current bacterial "kingdom" is a clade name (Pseudomonadati, Bacillati) and
cannot be used. Microbial eukaryotes such as *Babesia* have no kingdom at all.
The rule "Eukaryota and not Metazoa/Viridiplantae" handles both cases
correctly.
:::

::: {.decision}
**Cross-kingdom homonyms are kept apart.** In NCBI, *Bacillus* is both a bacterium
and a stick insect, and *Planococcus* is both a bacterium and a mealybug. Rows
are filtered to microbial scope *before* labels are deduplicated, so a bacterial
row can never inherit an insect lineage.
:::

```{r}
#| label: taxonomy
#| code-summary: "Scope classes and contaminant annotation"
lin <- rtsv("results", "taxonomy", "taxon_lineage.tsv")
tbl(lin[, .N, by = scope_class][order(-N)], "Distinct LCA taxa by scope")
tbl(lin[contaminant_flag == 1, .N, by = .(genus, contaminant_confidence)][order(-N)][1:20],
    "Reagent-contaminant genera flagged (first 20; annotation only)")
tbl(rtsv("results", "taxonomy", "homonyms.tsv"), "Cross-kingdom homonyms")
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false

show_code("metadata/reagent_contaminants.tsv", note = "the contaminant list used for annotation")
```

# The abundance matrices — steps 04, 04b and verification {#sec-matrices}

**This is the core join**, and the step the original project was missing. The
Pavian kreports counted **contigs**, so one contig counted as one "read" and a
300 bp contig at 2× scored the same as a 500 kb genome at 300×. Step 04 joins
each contig's LCA call to its read mapping and weights taxonomy by TPM.

Per sample:

1. inner-join `lca/<s>.blast.lca` × `mapping/<s>.coverage.tsv` on contig id;
2. apply the **contig evidence filter**: length ≥
   `r params$contig_filter$min_contig_len` bp, ≥
   `r params$contig_filter$min_mapped_reads` mapped reads, top bitscore ≥
   `r params$contig_filter$min_top_bitscore`;
3. renormalise TPM **within the microbial fraction** (`tpm_microbial`, summing
   to 10⁶ per sample);
4. aggregate to taxon and apply the presence thresholds;
5. export species / genus / family / phylum matrices.

::: {.decision}
**Short contigs are filtered *before* renormalising.** TPM divides by length,
so short, thinly covered contigs grab a disproportionate share. On sample
0143-F1-Am-sp, LCA-assigned contigs hold 95.4% of mapped *reads* but only
60.3% of *TPM*. Filtering first stops that assembly noise from setting the
denominator.
:::

## Where the sequence goes

```{r}
#| label: fractions
#| code-summary: "Per-sample fraction summary"
fr <- frac[, .(sample_id, contigs_total, contigs_passing_filter, reads_mapped_total,
               no_lca = tpm_pct_no_lca, filtered_out = tpm_pct_filtered_out,
               host = tpm_pct_host, bloodmeal = tpm_pct_bloodmeal,
               microbial = tpm_pct_microbial, ambiguous = tpm_pct_ambiguous)]
tbl(fr[, lapply(.SD, median), .SDcols = -1][, stat := "median across samples"],
    "Median % of each sample's TPM by fraction")
tbl(fr, "Per-sample fractions (% of TPM)")
```


```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 01c — also dropping contigs that failed the evidence filter: what actually reaches the analysis."
fig("01c_sequence_fractions_retained.png")
```

**How to read it.** The host share (`host`) badly *under*-states how much of
each library is tick, because tick DNA mostly gets no BLAST hit and lands in
`no_lca`. That is why the analysis renormalises within microbes and never uses
the host or no-hit share as a denominator.

## Does the evidence filter change the answer? (step 04b)

::: {.decision}
**The filter is a judgement call, so its effect is shown rather than asserted.**
The join is re-run under *lenient* / *default* / *strict* profiles.
:::

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity
#| code-summary: "Filter-sensitivity tables"
tbl(rtsv("results", "tables", "filter_sensitivity_fractions.tsv"),
    "Mean TPM shares under each filter profile")
fs <- rtsv("results", "tables", "filter_sensitivity_genera.tsv")
tbl(fs, "Top genera under each profile")
```

The dominant genera are robust to the choice. *Rickettsia* and *Francisella*
**grow** as the filter tightens, which is what real, deeply covered genomes do.
Taxa that vanish under *strict* (e.g. *Klebsiella*, *Iltovirus*) rest on thin
assemblies and deserve suspicion.

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
show_code("code/analysis/04_build_matrices.py", note = "the core join")
show_code("code/analysis/04b_filter_sensitivity.py")
show_code("code/analysis/verify.py", note = "assertions over the matrices")
```

# Sample metadata — steps 05, 05b and 06 {#sec-metadata}

**The curated source of truth is `metadata/barker_microbe_analysis_metadata.csv`**:
tick genus and species, life stage, number of ticks pooled, host type and
species, location, and GPS. The pipeline never edits it.

* **Step 05** builds a template with every field the pipeline can derive on its
  own. These are the sequencing run fields (flowcell, lane, index, which of two
  sequencing *submissions*) and *guesses* of species and stage parsed from the
  sample-id string.
* **Step 05b** joins the curated CSV to those derived fields and writes
  `metadata/sample_metadata.tsv`, which every later step reads.
* **Step 06** validates the result and stops the pipeline on errors that would
  otherwise become silent NAs.

::: {.decision}
**Step 05b fixes formatting only. It never changes content, and logs every
change.** Trailing spaces were stripped (`"fecialis "` → `"fecialis"`), and two
samples with `"lat, lon"` pasted into the latitude cell were split.
Biologically doubtful records are *flagged* for review in
`results/audit/metadata_import_issues.tsv`, never rewritten. The tick species
is written as a binomial (`Ixodes tasmani`). `species_identified = no` marks
`sp.` records, which count toward their genus but never toward a species-level
test.
:::

::: {.decision}
**The sequencing submission is kept as a covariate.** With no controls,
flowcell, lane and submission are the only handles on technical variation. They
are tested alongside the biology (sections 11 and 13).
:::

## Identifications corrected in this version

```{r}
#| label: id-corrections
#| code-summary: "Tick identifications changed since the previous run"
tbl(id_fix[order(sample_id)], "Curated tick species: previous run vs this run, with the curator's note")
```

`r nrow(id_fix[sample_id %in% excl$sample_id])` of these samples were also
removed (@sec-audit). Their corrected identifications are kept in the
metadata for the record.

## Records flagged for review

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Import issues"
iss <- rtsv("results", "audit", "metadata_import_issues.tsv")
tbl(iss[order(match(level, c("error", "review", "fixed", "info")))],
    "Everything step 05b changed or flagged")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Please check these against the source records
`r nrow(iss[level == "review"])` records are marked **review**. The mitogenome
cross-check in @sec-mito-check gives independent molecular evidence for or
against the species-level ones.
:::

```{r}

```

## What was sampled

```{r}
#| label: meta-overview
#| code-summary: "Cross-tabulations of the curated metadata (analysed samples)"
am <- meta[sample_id %in% mat_ids]
tbl(dcast(am[, .N, by = .(tick_genus, host_type)], tick_genus ~ host_type,
          value.var = "N", fill = 0), "Analysed samples: tick genus × host type")
tbl(am[, .N, by = .(tick_genus, tick_species)][order(tick_genus, -N)],
    "Analysed samples per tick species")

tbl(meta[, .(sample_id, status, tick_species, life_stage, n_ticks_pooled, host_type,
             host_species, collection_site, latitude, longitude, seq_submission)],
    "The full curated metadata as the pipeline sees it")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Tick genus and host type are confounded
*Amblyomma* in this collection is mostly from reptiles, while *Ixodes* and
*Haemaphysalis* are almost all from mammals. A naïve "host type" difference is
therefore largely a tick-genus difference. Section 13 tests host type
**within** tick genus for this reason.
:::

# The TreeSummarizedExperiment — step 07 {#sec-tse}

Assays, row data (taxonomy) and column data (metadata + per-sample QC) are
assembled into one Bioconductor `TreeSummarizedExperiment` per rank, at
`results/tse/`.

| assay | role |
|---|---|
| `tpm_microbial` | **the** abundance; sums to 10⁶ per sample |
| `reads` | evidence only: gates presence calls |
| `n_contigs` | evidence only |

::: {.decision}
**Higher ranks are agglomerated in R from the species object, then
cross-checked against the Python matrices.** Per-sample totals agree to within
0.0000 TPM at every rank, so there is one source of truth with two independent
implementations.
:::

**How to read figure 03.** Without blanks, this is the main contamination

## Cross-check against an independent classifier

```{r}
#| label: bracken
#| code-summary: "Concordance with read-level Kraken2/Bracken"
bc <- rtsv("results", "tables", "lca_vs_bracken_concordance.tsv")
```

The assembly → BLAST → LCA track and read-level Kraken2/Bracken share no
inputs beyond the reads. Across `r sum(!is.na(bc$spearman_rho))` samples, the
median per-sample Spearman correlation of genus abundances is
**ρ = `r round(median(bc$spearman_rho, na.rm = TRUE), 2)`**. This is moderate:
the two measure different things (assembled contigs vs raw reads) and disagree
most where assembly is poor. Low-abundance calls should be treated cautiously.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 05 — per-sample concordance between the LCA and Bracken genus profiles."
fig("05_lca_vs_bracken.png")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## The decontam frequency test was not run
`decontam`'s frequency method needs per-sample DNA concentrations, not blanks.
It is the one contamination test this design could support. No
`dna_conc_ng_ul` column exists in the metadata, so it was skipped. **Supplying
DNA concentrations is the single most useful addition to the metadata.**
:::

# Diversity, and how much is batch — step 09 {#sec-diversity}

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 06 — observed richness rises with assembly depth. Richness differences are partly technical."
fig("06_richness_vs_depth.png")
```

```{r}
#| label: alpha
#| code-summary: "Depth confound"
al <- rtsv("results", "tables", "alpha_diversity.tsv")
rho_depth <- cor(al$observed, al$contigs_passing, method = "spearman", use = "complete")
```

Spearman ρ between observed genera and contigs passing the filter is
**`r round(rho_depth, 2)`**, so richness is depth-confounded. Do not interpret
raw richness differences as biology.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 07 — alpha diversity by curated tick species; points coloured by tick genus."
fig("07_alpha_by_species.png")
```

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "Figure 08 — PCoA, Bray–Curtis, by tick species: one panel per tick genus (all other ticks in grey), species named at their centroid"
#|   - "Figure 08 — the same, Aitchison (CLR)"
fig("08_pcoa_bray_species.png"); fig("08_pcoa_aitchison_species.png")
```

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "Figure 09 — the same Bray–Curtis ordination by sequencing submission (colour and shape)"
#|   - "Figure 09 — Aitchison, by sequencing submission"
fig("09_pcoa_bray_batch.png"); fig("09_pcoa_aitchison_batch.png")
```

::: {.decision}
**Species are shown one genus at a time.** About thirty species cannot share
one colour scale and stay distinguishable. In figure 08 each panel is a tick
genus, its species are coloured within the panel and named on the plot, and
every other tick is drawn in grey for context.
:::

**Two distances, on purpose.** Bray–Curtis is driven by the dominant taxa.
Aitchison (Euclidean distance on centred log-ratios) treats the data as
compositional and weighs rare taxa more. A result that holds under both does not
depend on that choice.

```{r}
#| label: permanova-marginal
#| code-summary: "Single-term PERMANOVA, biology and batch in one table"
pm <- rtsv("results", "tables", "permanova.tsv")
tbl(pm, "PERMANOVA, each term tested alone (step 09)")
```

**How to read it.** R² is the share of between-sample variation the term
accounts for. Technical terms (`TECHNICAL`) are reported beside the biological
ones and *not* adjusted away. With no controls, a significant batch effect is
a finding, not a nuisance. These are single-term tests on all samples. The
tests in section 13 are better controlled.

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
show_code("code/analysis/09_diversity.R")
```

# Pathogen and endosymbiont targets — step 10 {#sec-targets}

A fixed list of `r nrow(fread(R("metadata", "target_taxa.tsv"), skip = "taxon\t"))` target taxa
(`metadata/target_taxa.tsv`) is mapped onto every sample. Each target is
categorised as *pathogen*, *endosymbiont*, *both*, or *uncertain*. Presence
is called on read and contig evidence, with a blunt evidence tier
(low / moderate / high) so a marginal call is never read as a firm one.

```{r}
#| label: targets
#| code-summary: "Target summary"
tbl(tsum[n_samples_present > 0, .(target, category, n_samples_present, prevalence_pct,
                                  median_tpm_when_present, longest_contig)],
    "Targets with at least one presence call")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## A genus-level hit in *Rickettsia*, *Francisella* or *Coxiella* does not establish pathogen presence
Each genus contains obligate tick endosymbionts **and** real pathogens
(spotted-fever-group rickettsiae, *F. tularensis*, *C. burnetii*). These are
near-identical over short contigs. Sections 15–16 resolve them with marker
genes. The same caution applies to *Borrelia* in Australia.
:::

The megabase-scale *Rickettsia*, *Francisella* and *Coxiella* contigs mean
near-complete genomes were recovered from the ticks that carry them.

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
show_code("code/analysis/10_export_targets.py")
show_code("metadata/target_taxa.tsv")
```

# Tick genus and species comparison — step 10b {#sec-tickgroups}

This section uses the curated metadata to ask four questions:

1. **Does microbial composition differ between tick genera, and between species
   within a genus?**
2. **Is any apparent host effect real once tick genus is accounted for?**
3. **Which endosymbionts does each tick lineage carry, and how dominant are
   they?** These maternally inherited symbionts are this study's keystone taxa.
4. **Does composition track geography?**

```{r}
#| label: tg-load
#| code-summary: "Load all step-10b tables"
TG <- function(f) rtsv("results", "tables", "tick_groups", f)
perm  <- TG("permanova.tsv");            pw   <- TG("permanova_pairwise_genus.tsv")
pg    <- TG("endosymbiont_prevalence_by_genus.tsv")
ps    <- TG("endosymbiont_prevalence_by_species.tsv")
fish  <- TG("endosymbiont_fisher_tests.tsv"); kw <- TG("endosymbiont_abundance_kruskal.tsv")
dom   <- TG("dominant_genus_per_sample.tsv"); co <- TG("endosymbiont_cooccurrence.tsv")
ind   <- TG("indicator_genera_by_tick_genus.tsv"); mant <- TG("mantel_composition_vs_geography.tsv")
MIN_N <- params$tick_groups$min_samples_per_group
# One PERMANOVA row by test name and distance. The arguments are deliberately
# NOT called `test`/`distance`: inside data.table's [ ] those names would
# resolve to the columns themselves and silently match every row.
P <- function(which_test, which_dist = "bray") {
  x <- perm[perm$test == which_test & perm$distance == which_dist]
  stopifnot(nrow(x) == 1)
  x
}
# p-values as plain text (knitr would otherwise render 7.8e-05 as 7.8^{-5})
fp <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, format(signif(p, 2), scientific = TRUE), sprintf("%.3f", p))
```

::: {.decision}
**Groups with fewer than `r MIN_N` samples are drawn but never tested.**
Single ticks are shown so nothing is hidden. A "species mean" of one tick is
an individual, not a species.
:::

::: {.decision}
**PERMDISP is reported beside every single-factor PERMANOVA.** PERMANOVA
responds to differences in *spread* as well as *location*. A significant
PERMANOVA together with a significant PERMDISP means part of the "difference"
is that one group is more variable.
:::

::: {.decision}
**Host type is tested *within* tick genus.** Permutations are restricted to
within-genus blocks, so the test only uses host contrasts that occur inside a
genus (e.g. *Amblyomma* on reptiles vs mammals). A marginal model,
`~ genus + host + submission` with `by = "margin"`, gives each term's share
*after* the others.
:::

```{r}
fig("10_samples_by_tick_and_host.png")
```

```{r}
fig("11a_composition_by_tick_genus.png")
```

## Do tick genera and species differ in composition?

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "Figure 12 — PCoA (Bray–Curtis). Colour = tick genus (also labelled directly), ellipses = 68% for genera with n ≥ 3."
#|   - "Figure 12 — the same, Aitchison distance."
fig("12_pcoa_bray_tick_genus.png"); fig("12_pcoa_aitchison_tick_genus.png")
```

```{r}
#| label: permanova-groups
#| code-summary: "All step-10b PERMANOVA tests"
tbl(perm[, .(test, distance, term, n, levels, R2, F, p, dispersion_p, note)],
    "PERMANOVA (999 permutations). dispersion_p = PERMDISP for the same grouping.", page = 40)
```

```{r}
#| label: permanova-text
#| echo: false
g_b  <- P("tick genus", "bray");      g_a  <- P("tick genus", "aitchison")
sg_b <- P("tick species | genus", "bray"); sg_a <- P("tick species | genus", "aitchison")
h_b  <- P("host type", "bray");       hg_b <- P("host type | genus", "bray")
hg_a <- P("host type | genus", "aitchison")
mm_b <- perm[test == "marginal model" & distance == "bray"]
f3 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
f2 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
```

**What the tests say** (Bray–Curtis; Aitchison in brackets):

* **Tick genus**: R² = `r f2(g_b$R2)`, *p* = `r f3(g_b$p)`
  [R² = `r f2(g_a$R2)`, *p* = `r f3(g_a$p)`]; PERMDISP *p* =
  `r f3(g_b$dispersion_p)`.
* **Species within genus** (species fitted after genus, permutations within
  genus): R² = `r f2(sg_b$R2)`, *p* = `r f3(sg_b$p)`
  [R² = `r f2(sg_a$R2)`, *p* = `r f3(sg_a$p)`].
* **Host type, ignoring genus**: R² = `r f2(h_b$R2)`, *p* = `r f3(h_b$p)`.
  **Host type within genus**: R² = `r f2(hg_b$R2)`, *p* = `r f3(hg_b$p)`
  [*p* = `r f3(hg_a$p)`].
* **Marginal model** (each term after the others):
  `r paste(sprintf("%s R² = %s, p = %s", mm_b$term, f2(mm_b$R2), f3(mm_b$p)), collapse = "; ")`.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What this means
* **Tick genus is the strongest structure in the data.** It explains about
  `r round(100 * g_b$R2)`% of between-tick variation (Bray–Curtis), far more
  than host type or sequencing batch. PERMDISP is also significant, so genera
  differ in how *variable* their microbiomes are as well as in what they
  contain. *Haemaphysalis* in particular forms a tight, distinct cluster
  (figure 12).
* **Species matter beyond genus**, but less. That holds clearly under
  Bray–Curtis, which is driven by the dominant symbionts. Under Aitchison, which
  up-weights rare taxa, it is borderline. Species differences are therefore
  mostly about *which dominant symbiont* a tick carries.
* **Host type is a small effect once tick genus is accounted for.** Its
  within-genus R² is ~`r round(100 * hg_b$R2)`%, and in the marginal model it
  is significant under Bray–Curtis but not under Aitchison. Most of the naïve
  host-type signal is the genus × host confound.
* **Sequencing submission is a small but real batch effect** in both
  distances (marginal R² ≈ `r round(100 * mm_b[term == "seq_submission"]$R2)`%).
  Report it; do not adjust it away.
* **Life stage has no detectable effect** within genus.
:::

```{r}
#| label: pairwise
#| code-summary: "Pairwise genus PERMANOVA"
tbl(pw[order(distance, p_adj_BH)], "Pairwise PERMANOVA between tick genera (BH-adjusted within distance)")
```

## Endosymbionts: the keystone symbionts of each tick lineage

::: {.decision}
**"Keystone" here means the dominant, maternally inherited symbionts.** These are
the taxa that define a tick lineage's microbiome. Keystone taxa were *not*
inferred from co-occurrence-network centrality. With 3–56 samples per genus,
compositional abundances and no controls, network inference is unreliable. The
same questions are answered directly instead: which symbiont each lineage
carries (prevalence), how dominant it is (abundance when present, dominant genus
per tick), and which symbionts exclude or accompany each other (co-occurrence).
:::

::: {.decision}
**Presence uses the step-10 call (reads + contigs), never TPM alone.**
*Rickettsia*, *Francisella* and *Coxiella* are genus-level calls, marked `*` in
every figure.
:::

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 13a — endosymbiont prevalence per tick genus; cells give ticks with a presence call / ticks analysed."
fig("13a_endosymbiont_prevalence_by_genus.png")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 13b — endosymbiont prevalence per tick species."
fig("13b_endosymbiont_prevalence_by_species.png")
```

```{r}
#| label: prev-tables
#| code-summary: "Prevalence with 95% Wilson intervals"
tbl(pg[n_present > 0][order(target, -prevalence_pct)],
    "Endosymbiont prevalence by tick genus (Wilson 95% CI)", page = 15)
tbl(ps[n_present > 0][order(target, genus, -prevalence_pct)],
    "Endosymbiont prevalence by tick species")
```

```{r}
#| label: fisher
#| code-summary: "Fisher's exact tests on presence/absence"
tbl(fish, "Endosymbiont presence vs tick genus / species / host type (BH-adjusted across all tests)")
```

**How to read the Fisher table.** "tick genus" asks whether prevalence differs
across the genera with n ≥ `r MIN_N`. "species within X" asks the same among
the species of one genus. "host type within X" asks whether, inside one tick
genus, ticks from different host types differ. That separates a host effect
from a tick effect. Tables larger than 2×2 use Monte-Carlo *p*-values
(`r format(params$tick_groups$fisher_B, big.mark = ",")` replicates).

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 14 — how dominant each endosymbiont is in the ticks that carry it (% of microbial TPM, log scale; shape = host type)."
fig("14_endosymbiont_abundance_by_genus.png")
```

```{r}
#| label: kw
#| code-summary: "Kruskal–Wallis: endosymbiont abundance across tick genera"
tbl(kw, "Kruskal–Wallis test of endosymbiont relative abundance across tick genera (all ticks, zeros included)")
```

```{r}
#| label: endo-text
#| echo: false
pv <- function(g, t) { x <- pg[genus == g & target == t]
  sprintf("%d/%d (%s)", x$n_present, x$n, pct(x$prevalence_pct, 0)) }
cxf <- co[target_a == "Coxiella" & target_b == "Francisella"]
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## What this means: each tick lineage has its own primary symbiont
* ***Coxiella*** is the symbiont of *Bothriocroton*
  (`r pv("Bothriocroton", "Coxiella")`) and the soft ticks: *Argas*
  `r pv("Argas", "Coxiella")`, *Ornithodoros* `r pv("Ornithodoros", "Coxiella")`.
  It is nearly absent from *Amblyomma* (`r pv("Amblyomma", "Coxiella")`) and
  absent from *Haemaphysalis* (`r pv("Haemaphysalis", "Coxiella")`).
* ***Francisella*** takes its place in *Amblyomma*
  (`r pv("Amblyomma", "Francisella")`) and *Haemaphysalis*
  (`r pv("Haemaphysalis", "Francisella")`).
* **The two rarely share a tick.** They co-occur in only `r cxf$n_both` ticks,
  odds ratio `r round(cxf$odds_ratio, 2)` (*p* = `r fp(cxf$p)`). This
  matches the known replacement of *Coxiella*-like by *Francisella*-like
  primary symbionts in ticks. Stratified by tick genus, the exclusion weakens
  (*p* = `r fp(cxf$p_genus_stratified)`). It is therefore mostly a
  *between-genus* partition, with little evidence yet of exclusion inside a
  genus.
* ***Arsenophonus*** is essentially an *Amblyomma* associate
  (`r pv("Amblyomma", "Arsenophonus")`), and differs among *Amblyomma*
  species.
* ***Ixodes*** carries a mixed set: *Rickettsiella*
  (`r pv("Ixodes", "Rickettsiella")`), *Rickettsia*
  (`r pv("Ixodes", "Rickettsia")`), *Midichloria*
  (`r pv("Ixodes", "Midichloria")`) and *Wolbachia*
  (`r pv("Ixodes", "Wolbachia")`). *Wolbachia* in ticks usually comes from
  parasitoid wasps.
* ***Rickettsia*** is widespread across hard-tick genera. Its genus-level call
  cannot separate endosymbiont from spotted-fever-group pathogen (@sec-trees).
:::

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 15 — the single most abundant microbial genus in each tick, tallied per tick species."
fig("15_dominant_genus_by_tick_species.png")
```

**How to read figure 15.** The dominant genus is often *not* a symbiont.
Examples are the Jingmen-like flavivirus (`Flaviviridae (unresolved)`), which
dominates `r dom[genus == "Haemaphysalis" & dominant == "Flaviviridae (unresolved)", .N]`
of `r dom[genus == "Haemaphysalis", .N]` *Haemaphysalis*;
`unresolved` bins; and genera on the reagent-contaminant list (e.g.
*Elizabethkingia*, *Pseudomonas*, *Stenotrophomonas*). A contaminant topping a
tick usually means that tick had little symbiont signal, so a small
contaminating load ranks first after renormalising. Read those ticks as
"no dominant symbiont detected", not as contaminant-driven microbiomes.

```{r}
#| label: dominant
#| code-summary: "Dominant genus per tick genus"
dsum <- dom[, .N, by = .(genus, dominant)][, share := N / sum(N), by = genus][order(genus, -N)]
tbl(dsum[, .SD[1:min(3, .N)], by = genus], "Top three dominant microbial genera per tick genus")
tbl(dom, "Dominant microbial genus in every tick")
```

## Do endosymbionts co-occur or exclude each other?

::: {.decision}
**Co-occurrence is tested twice**: across all ticks, and stratified by tick
genus (exact Mantel–Haenszel). Two symbionts that simply favour the same tick
genus look associated in the first test but not in the second. The stratified
result is the one to interpret.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cooc
#| code-summary: "Pairwise co-occurrence"
tbl(co, "Endosymbiont co-occurrence: odds ratio > 1 = found together more than expected")
```

## Indicator genera: what characterises each tick genus?

Indicator-value analysis (IndVal.g, `indicspecies::multipatt`) scores each
microbial genus on **specificity** (A: how concentrated its abundance is in one
tick genus) and **fidelity** (B: how many ticks of that genus carry it).
Candidate genera must pass the read threshold in ≥
`r 100 * params$tick_groups$indicator_min_prevalence`% of ticks.

```{r}
#| label: indicators
#| code-summary: "Indicator genera"
if (is.null(ind)) cat("*indicspecies was not available when step 10b ran; re-run it once installed.*") else
  tbl(ind[p_adj_BH < 0.05], "Significant indicator genera (BH q < 0.05); flagged_contaminant = on the reagent list")
```

## Does composition track geography?

```{r}
#| label: mantel
#| code-summary: "Mantel tests: composition vs great-circle distance"
tbl(mant, "Mantel test (Spearman) of microbial dissimilarity vs geographic distance (km)")
```

**How to read it.** Across all ticks, distance is confounded with tick genus and
host, because different tick genera were collected in different regions. The
**within-genus and within-species rows** ask the clean question: do two ticks of
the same species have more similar microbiomes when they were collected closer
together?

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
show_code("code/analysis/10b_tick_group_comparison.R", note = "every test in this section")
```

# Marker genes for the targets — steps 11–16 {#sec-markers}

**Why.** Step 10 says a genus is present. For *Rickettsia*, *Coxiella* and
*Francisella*, the question is *which species*: endosymbiont or pathogen.
16S rRNA cannot answer that, so each target has its own panel of discriminating
loci (`metadata/target_markers.tsv`). Examples: `gltA`, `ompA`, `ompB` and
`sca4` for *Rickettsia*; `rpoB` and `icd` for *Coxiella*; `msp4` for
*Anaplasma*; `cox1` and `cytb` for piroplasms.

::: {.decision}
**Every target contig is searched, not just confident detections.** A recovered
marker gene is itself detection evidence. The step-10 call travels with each
sequence as an annotation, so you can filter afterwards.
:::

::: {.decision}
**Paralogues are resolved competitively.** *Rickettsia* `ompA`, `ompB` and
`sca4` are all Sca-family autotransporters and cross-hit one another's probes.
Without resolution, one stretch of contig would be exported three times under
three gene names. The best single-probe bitscore claims the region, and the
loser is kept in `marker_loci.tsv` as `paralog_suppressed`.
:::

::: {.decision}
**Reading frames are recovered from the sequence, and internal stops are
flagged, not fixed.** Sequences with stops go to `*.flagged.fna` and stay out
of the alignments. Protein-coding loci are aligned as amino acids and
back-translated, which gives a true codon alignment.
:::

::: {.decision}
**Viral targets are probed with the viruses actually present, not the
family type species.** The `Flaviviridae` signal is almost entirely a
*segmented* Jingmen-like virus with no polyprotein. Classical flavivirus
probes found nothing, while Jingmenvirus segment probes recovered VP1/VP2 at
83% identity.
:::

```{r}
#| label: markers
#| code-summary: "Marker recovery"
ms <- rtsv("results", "markers", "marker_summary.tsv")
tbl(ms, "Recovered marker loci per target (step 16)")
tbl(rtsv("results", "markers", "marker_gaps.tsv"), "Loci that produced nothing, and why")
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
for (f in c("11_fetch_marker_refs.py", "12_extract_target_contigs.py", "13_find_markers.py",
            "14_extract_markers.py", "15_align_markers.py", "16_marker_report.py",
            "markers_lib.py"))
  show_code(file.path("code", "analysis", f))
show_code("metadata/target_markers.tsv", note = "the marker panel")
show_code("run_markers.sh")
```

# Marker-gene trees — steps 17–19b {#sec-trees}

Steps 17–19 download named-species references for every recovered locus, cut
the locus out of them, align them with the tick sequences, and build a FastTree
per locus.

::: {.decision}
**References are chosen for breadth, not depth.** Candidates are screened on
title before download, and the quota is spread round-robin across organisms
(≤ `r params$trees$curate$max_per_organism` per organism). Otherwise forty
copies of *R. felis* `gltA` would crowd out the species that give a tree its
topology.
:::

::: {.decision}
**Nothing is trusted until it is blasted.** Every downloaded record is
searched with the locus probes, only the hit region is kept, and a reference
whose locus carries an internal stop is dropped.
:::

::: {.decision}
**Tip labels use the curated metadata.** The tick species stored inside a
sample's sequence name was frozen when step 12 ran, often from the id-string
guess. Step 19b now labels each figure from `metadata/sample_metadata.tsv`, so
the trees show current identifications without re-running the BLAST steps.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## These are screening trees
FastTree with SH-like local support is fast and approximate. SH-like values
are **not** bootstrap support. Many tick sequences are gene fragments: a
300 bp `gltA` fragment inside a clade tells you the genus and the clade, not
the species. Rebuild the loci that matter under a model-tested IQ-TREE
analysis (step 25 shows the pattern).
:::

```{r}
#| label: tree-summary
#| code-summary: "Tree summary"
ts <- rtsv("results", "markers", "trees", "tree_summary.tsv")
tbl(ts[, .(target, marker, n_tips, n_samples, n_refs, n_organisms, aln_cols,
           median_ungapped_nt, pct_gaps, tree_built, note)], "Every locus: tips, references, alignment")
```

```{r}
#| label: tree-figures
#| results: asis
#| code-summary: "Every tree figure, grouped by target"
pngs <- sort(list.files(R("results", "markers", "trees"), pattern = "\\.png$",
                        recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE))
pngs <- pngs[!grepl("/refs/|/hits/", pngs)]
if (!length(pngs)) cat("*No tree figures yet: run `Rscript code/analysis/19b_tree_figures.R`.*\n")
for (tg in unique(basename(dirname(pngs)))) {
  cat(sprintf("\n## *%s* {.unnumbered}\n\n::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n", tg))
  for (p in pngs[basename(dirname(pngs)) == tg]) {
    cat(sprintf("### %s\n\n![](%s){width=100%%}\n\n",
                sub(".*__", "", sub("\\.png$", "", basename(p))),
                sub(paste0("^", ROOT), "..", p)))
  }
  cat(":::\n\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
for (f in c("17_fetch_tree_refs.py", "18_curate_tree_refs.py", "19_build_trees.py",
            "19b_tree_figures.R", "trees_lib.py"))
  show_code(file.path("code", "analysis", f))
show_code("metadata/tree_references.tsv"); show_code("metadata/tree_ref_genomes.tsv")
```

# The ticks' own mitogenome phylogeny — steps 20–26 {#sec-mito}

```{r}
#| label: mito-refs-load
#| code-summary: "Load the reference-mitogenome panel and step 20b's results"
refpanel <- fread(R("metadata", "mito_ref_genomes.tsv"), skip = "accession", na.strings = c("", "NA"))
refsum   <- rtsv("results", "mito", "ref_genomes", "ref_genome_summary.tsv")
n_ref_ok <- sum(refsum$status == "ok")
n_raw    <- length(grep("\\S", readLines(R("results", "mito", "mito_ref_seqs.txt")), value = TRUE))
psum     <- rtsv("results", "mito", "concat", "mito_partition_summary.tsv")
n_concat <- length(grep("^>", readLines(R("results", "mito", "concat", "mito_concat.fasta"))))
```

An independent workflow builds a phylogeny of the **ticks themselves** from
their mitochondrial genomes:

1. take one mitogenome contig per sample, chosen by homology;
2. download **`r n_ref_ok` published tick mitogenomes** of named species
   (step 20b) and annotate them the same way;
3. annotate the 13 protein-coding genes;
4. align each gene separately, codon-aware, samples and references together;
5. infer one partitioned maximum-likelihood tree in IQ-TREE, with ModelFinder
   choosing a model per gene and 1000 ultrafast bootstrap and SH-aLRT
   replicates, rooted on the Argasidae references.


## The samples' mitogenomes — steps 21–22 {#sec-mito-samples}

::: {.decision}
**Homology search is protein-level and order-wide.** Hard and soft ticks
diverged more than 200 Mya, and nucleotide BLAST misses genes at that distance.
tblastn on the conserved proteins finds them. A COX1 hit at 41.5% identity
with *E* = 5×10⁻¹⁰⁷ is real. The identity floor was lowered and the *E*-value
does the gating.
:::

::: {.decision}
**The invertebrate mitochondrial genetic code (NCBI table 5) is used
throughout.** Under the standard code, every in-frame TGA (Trp here) reads as
a stop, and most real genes would be flagged as broken.
:::

::: {.decision}
**No cross-gene "paralogue" resolution for mitogenomes.** Porting it from the
marker workflow silently deleted a correct ND1 call in 87 of 149 samples,
because ND1's approximate boundary overlapped its neighbour rrnL by a few base
pairs. Mitochondrial genes are single-copy, so there is nothing to resolve.
:::

::: {.decision}
**MITOS2 is installed but not used.** Its reference data is hosted only on
Zenodo, which this compute node cannot reach. Annotation uses the homology
fallback, which gives no tRNAs, gene order or exact start/stop codons. The
code switches to MITOS2 automatically if `mito.annotate.mitos_refdata_dir` is
set.
:::

```{r}
#| label: mito-selection
#| code-summary: "Mitogenome recovery per sample"
sel <- rtsv("results", "mito", "mito_selection.tsv")
tbl(sel[, .N, by = status], "Mitogenome candidate outcome")
tbl(sel[, .(sample_id, status, n_candidate_contigs, contig_len, n_genes_found, genes_found)],
    "Per-sample mitogenome recovery")
```

## Published reference mitogenomes — step 20b {#sec-mito-refs}

Without references, the tree could only say which samples resemble each other.
With them, every sample sits among species of known identity, and the tree
has a defensible root. The raw list supplied
(`results/mito/mito_ref_seqs.txt`, `r n_raw` lines) was curated into
`metadata/mito_ref_genomes.tsv`: one row per distinct accession, every listed
line accounted for, and a reason for anything not used. `r n_ref_ok`
mitogenomes were downloaded, passed the identity check and were annotated.

::: {.callout-important}
## Errors found in the supplied list
* **`NC_028521`, listed as *Dermacentor nuttalli*, is a frog** (*Rana
  huanrensis*). It was replaced with `NC_028528`, the *D. nuttalli* RefSeq
  mitogenome (a one-digit typo).
* **`MT371800`, listed as *D. taiwanensis*, is *D. bellulus* in GenBank.**
  It is used and labelled as listed. Please confirm which name is intended.
* Truncated or garbled accessions were resolved to the only matching record
  (table below). `KY45753` (*R. evertsi*) matches two clones from one study;
  `KY457537` was used.
* Three RefSeq copies duplicated GenBank records already in the list and were
  dropped, as were ~15 accessions listed twice.
* Two entries are SRA read runs, not genomes (`SRR4301110` *A. aureolatum*,
  `SRR8074777` *A.* aff. *moreliae*). They are not used. Each would need its
  mitogenome assembled from reads first.
:::

```{r}
#| label: mito-refs-curation
#| code-summary: "Every panel row that was corrected, dropped or needs a check"
tbl(refpanel[!is.na(note) & note != "", .(accession, use, species, listed_as, note)],
    "Reference list: corrections, exclusions and notes", page = 40)
```

::: {.decision}
**Every reference is checked against its GenBank title before use.** Step 20b
refuses a record whose title lacks the expected species epithet. That check
catches errors like the frog automatically.
:::

::: {.decision}
**References are annotated like the samples, not from GenBank features.** The
same tblastn/blastn search, locus merging, reading-frame and stop-trim code
(step 21's functions, `frame_mito_pcg`) runs on every reference. Many listed
records (the Kelava et al. `MT3718xx` series) are GenBank "UNVERIFIED"
sequences with no gene features. Identical gene-boundary rules also keep the
codon alignments free of an artificial references-versus-samples edge
pattern. A reference gene with internal stops is left out, not flagged: in a
published complete genome it means a mis-called locus.
:::

::: {.decision}
**The tree is rooted on the Argasidae references only.** The split between
soft ticks (Argasidae) and hard ticks (Ixodidae) is the deepest
well-established node among living ticks. Only *reference* tips define the
outgroup, so a mislabelled sample cannot move the root. *Nuttalliella
namaqua* is deliberately left out of the outgroup, because its position
relative to the two families is the contested question.
:::

```{r}
#| label: mito-refs-genes
#| code-summary: "Gene recovery in the references and in the final matrix"
tbl(refsum[status == "ok", .(accession, family, species, length, n_pcg, genes_annotated, flagged_genes)],
    "Reference mitogenomes used: protein-coding genes recovered by the homology method")
tbl(psum, "The supermatrix: one partition per protein-coding gene, samples and references")
```

The references expose a limit of the method. On complete published genomes,
homology search recovers **ATP8 in `r psum[gene == "ATP8"]$n_refs_with_gene`
of `r n_ref_ok`** and **ND6 in `r psum[gene == "ND6"]$n_refs_with_gene`**. These
are the same two genes the samples most often lack. Their absence from a
sample is a detection limit for short or divergent genes, not evidence that
the sequence is missing. The final matrix has `r n_concat` rows
(`r n_concat - n_ref_ok` samples + `r n_ref_ok` references) and
`r n_(max(psum$end))` columns.

## The tree — steps 23–26 {#sec-mito-tree}

```{r}
#| label: mito-tree-facts
#| code-summary: "Tree facts quoted below: rooting, Nuttalliella, reference genera"
mtree  <- read.tree(R("results", "mito", "tree", "mito.treefile"))
tsid   <- sub("[|].*", "", mtree$tip.label)
rinfo  <- refsum[status == "ok"][match(tsid, ref_id)]          # NA rows = samples
fam    <- rinfo$family
# References only: do they reproduce the accepted higher-level tick taxonomy?
rt   <- keep.tip(mtree, mtree$tip.label[!is.na(fam)])
rfam <- fam[!is.na(fam)][match(rt$tip.label, mtree$tip.label[!is.na(fam)])]
rgen <- rinfo$genus[!is.na(fam)][match(rt$tip.label, mtree$tip.label[!is.na(fam)])]
rt   <- root(rt, outgroup = rt$tip.label[rfam == "Argasidae"], resolve.root = TRUE)
nut_ixo   <- rt$tip.label[rfam %in% c("Ixodidae", "Nuttalliellidae")]
nut_sister <- is.monophyletic(rt, nut_ixo)
nut_supp  <- rt$node.label[getMRCA(rt, nut_ixo) - Ntip(rt)]
ixo_mono  <- is.monophyletic(rt, rt$tip.label[rfam == "Ixodidae"])
gen_mono  <- rbindlist(lapply(unique(rgen), function(g) {
  w <- rt$tip.label[rgen == g]
  if (length(w) < 2) return(NULL)
  data.table(genus = g, n_refs = length(w), monophyletic = is.monophyletic(rt, w))
}))
# terminal branch of every tip, to spot long-branch samples
tb <- setNames(mtree$edge.length[match(seq_along(tsid), mtree$edge[, 2])], tsid)
mv  <- rtsv("results", "mito", "tables", "mito_vs_metadata.tsv")
og_n <- uniqueN(refsum[status == "ok" & family == "Argasidae"]$ref_id)
# the outgroup clade as steps 26/26b root it: the smallest clade holding every
# Argasidae reference, found with the tree rooted on a non-argasid reference
t0 <- root(mtree, outgroup = mtree$tip.label[which(fam == "Ixodidae")[1]], resolve.root = TRUE)
og_clade <- sub("[|].*", "", extract.clade(t0, getMRCA(t0, t0$tip.label[fam[match(t0$tip.label, mtree$tip.label)] %in% "Argasidae"]))$tip.label)
og_samp  <- mv[sample_id %in% og_clade]
og_soft  <- og_samp[tick_genus %in% c("Argas", "Ornithodoros", "Alectorobius")]
og_other <- og_samp[!tick_genus %in% c("Argas", "Ornithodoros", "Alectorobius")]
```

The partitioned ML tree has `r Ntip(mtree)` tips: `r sum(is.na(fam))` samples
and `r sum(!is.na(fam))` references. It is rooted on the clade holding the
`r og_n` Argasidae references, which also holds `r nrow(og_soft)`
soft-tick samples and `r nrow(og_other)` samples curated as
`r paste0("*", unique(og_other$tick_genus), "*", collapse = "/")`
(`r paste0("\x60", og_other$sample_id, "\x60", collapse = ", ")`; see below).

**The references reproduce the accepted tick phylogeny, which is the check
that the tree can be trusted at depth:**

* Ixodidae is `r if (ixo_mono) "monophyletic" else "**not** monophyletic"`.
* *Nuttalliella namaqua* is `r if (nut_sister) "sister to Ixodidae" else "**not** sister to Ixodidae"`
  (SH-aLRT/UFBoot `r nut_supp`). This agrees with published mitogenome
  analyses that place Nuttalliellidae closest to the hard ticks.
* `r sum(gen_mono$monophyletic)` of `r nrow(gen_mono)` reference genera with
  ≥ 2 references are monophyletic. The exceptions are
  `r paste0("*", gen_mono[monophyletic == FALSE]$genus, "*", collapse = " and ")`.
  Both are known: *Ornithodoros* in the broad sense is paraphyletic with
  respect to *Alectorobius* and other argasid genera, and the *Alloceraea*
  species (*H. inermis*, *H. kitaokai*) fall outside the rest of
  *Haemaphysalis*.

```{r}
#| label: mito-ref-genera
#| code-summary: "Monophyly of each reference genus (references only)"
tbl(gen_mono, "Reference genera in the mitogenome tree (samples pruned)")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 17 — the partitioned ML mitogenome tree, rooted on the Argasidae clade. Published references in black bold (species and accession); the square at each sample tip is its tick genus (as named when step 21 ran, i.e. from the corrected metadata). Node labels SH-aLRT/UFBoot."
include_graphics(REL("results", "mito", "figures", "mito_tree.png"))
```

## Do the curated identifications agree with the mitogenome tree? — step 26b {#sec-mito-check}

The mitogenome tree is **independent molecular evidence** of what each tick
is. Step 26b relabels every sample tip from the *curated* metadata and asks
three questions:

1. **What is the selected contig?** Its own nt-BLAST LCA from the main
   pipeline (`lca/`) is looked up. Since step 21 now accepts only tick contigs,
   the verdict `NOT_TICK_CONTIG` should never appear; it remains as a check.
2. **Do its nearest relatives agree?** The 3 nearest tips by patristic
   distance, samples or references, vote on genus and species.
3. **What is the nearest named reference?** The closest reference tip, the
   nearest thing to a named-species identification this tree gives.

It also tests whether each curated genus and species is monophyletic, with
the references of that name included.

::: {.callout-note}
## A disagreement is not automatically a metadata error
The mitogenome is picked by homology from a whole-tick assembly. A disagreement
can also mean the wrong contig was chosen: a contaminating tick's
mitogenome, a NUMT, the host's mitogenome, or a sparse sample on a long
branch. Check `n_genes`, `nn1_dist` and `contig_lca` before deciding.
:::

```{r}
#| label: mito-check
#| code-summary: "Concordance between the curated metadata and the mitogenome tree"
old_mv <- rtsv("results", "mito", "samples_only", "mito_vs_metadata.tsv")
print(kable(mv[, .N, by = verdict][order(verdict)], caption = "Concordance verdicts (tree with references)"))
if (!is.null(old_mv)) {
  cmp <- merge(old_mv[, .(sample_id, samples_only = verdict)], mv[, .(sample_id, with_refs = verdict)],
               by = "sample_id", all = TRUE)
  kable(dcast(cmp[, .N, by = .(samples_only, with_refs)], samples_only ~ with_refs, value.var = "N", fill = 0),
        caption = "How each sample's verdict changed when the references were added (rows: samples-only tree)")
}
```

### Only tick contigs can be selected (step 21)

```{r}
#| label: mito-gate
#| code-summary: "Which contigs the tick-LCA gate rejected"
gate <- sel[, .(sample_id, status, selected_contig_lca, selected_contig_lca_class,
                n_gene_contigs, n_non_tick_excluded, n_genes_found)]
tbl(sel[, .N, by = .(status, selected_contig_lca_class)][order(status)],
    "Step-21 outcome, by the LCA class of the selected contig")
tbl(sel[status == "no_tick_contig", .(sample_id, tick_species, n_gene_contigs, non_tick_excluded)],
    "Samples whose mitochondrial genes were found only on non-tick contigs")
```

The tick probes cannot tell a tick mitogenome from a vertebrate one: a
blood-meal host's mitogenome carries the same 13 genes and clears the *E*-value
gate. In the previous run this made step 21 pick the host's mitogenome
(*Varanus*, *Petrogale*, *Isoodon*) or a bacterial contig with three weak hits
for 7 samples, which then sat on very long branches outside every tick genus.

::: {.decision}
**A candidate contig must be a tick by its own nt-BLAST LCA.** Step 21 now
looks up every candidate contig in the sample's `lca/` file and accepts only
contigs whose LCA is inside Ixodida (`mito.candidates.lca_filter`). A contig
with **no** nt hit stays eligible but ranks below confirmed tick contigs:
complete *Ornithodoros* mitogenomes here have no nt hit, because nt holds no
close relative. Among eligible contigs, ties in gene count are broken by
**coverage**, before bitscore. In a mixed tube, bitscore only says which tick
is closer to the probe set, while coverage says which tick contributed most of
the DNA.
:::

`r sum(sel$status == "no_tick_contig")` samples now have no tick mitogenome
contig at all (table above). No selected contig is classified as non-tick
(`r sum(mv$verdict == "NOT_TICK_CONTIG")` `NOT_TICK_CONTIG` verdicts).

### Do the curated identifications agree with the tree?

```{r}
#| label: mito-discordant
#| code-summary: "Genus- and species-discordant samples, with the nearest reference and the contig's own LCA"
gd <- mv[verdict == "GENUS_DISCORDANT"]
tbl(mv[verdict %in% c("GENUS_DISCORDANT", "species_discordant"),
       .(sample_id, tick_species, verdict, n_genes, nn1, nn1_species, nn1_dist,
         nearest_ref_species, nearest_ref_dist, contig_lca)],
    "Samples whose curated identification disagrees with their nearest relatives in the tree")
```

A sample is genus-discordant when its 3 nearest tips outvote its curated
genus, **or** when two independent lines agree against it: the contig's own
nt-BLAST genus and the genus of the nearest reference. The second rule exists
because the vote has a blind spot. Two tubes holding the *same* foreign tick's
mitogenome sit together and vote for each other's curated genus.

`r nrow(gd)` samples are genus-discordant in this run, against 19 before the
review. Most of the earlier ones were either removed (@sec-audit) or had their
identification corrected (@sec-metadata).

### Contaminant, mixture or wrong tick? — step 26c {#sec-mito-audit}

```{r}
#| label: mito-audit
#| code-summary: "Step 26c: the nuclear-rRNA test of every discordant sample"
aud <- rtsv("results", "mito", "tables", "mito_discordance_audit.tsv")
sig <- rtsv("results", "mito", "tables", "tick_genus_signal.tsv")
aud_pre <- rtsv("results", "_pre_exclusion_20261008", "mito", "tables", "mito_discordance_audit.tsv")
if (!is.null(aud)) {
  tbl(aud[, .N, by = call][order(-N)], "Step-26c calls in this run")
  tbl(aud[, .(sample_id, curated_genus, mito_status, mito_genus, rrna_top, rrna_curated_share,
              mito_hits_top, nearest_sample, nearest_sample_pdist, nearest_same_run, call,
              exclude_from_mito_tree, exclude_from_species_analyses, reason)],
      "Every audited sample")
}
```

A genus-discordant mitogenome does not say *why* it is discordant. The tube
may hold another tick altogether, or two ticks, or the right tick plus a trace
of another tick's DNA that happened to assemble better. Step 26c asks the
sample's own raw nt BLAST an independent question: **which tick genus do its
nuclear rRNA contigs (18S, 28S, 5.8S, ITS) belong to?**

::: {.decision}
**Only high-identity hits, split by subject type, are counted.** The obvious
measure, the share of all tick BLAST hits going to each genus, does not work.
nt holds whole nuclear genomes for only a few tick genera, so in a correctly
labelled *Amblyomma* or *Bothriocroton* sample ~70% of tick hits go to
*Dermacentor* and ~1% to the curated genus. That share measures nt, not the
tick. Tick nuclear rRNA and mitochondrial genes are in nt for nearly every
genus, though, and at ≥ `r params$mito$audit$min_pident`% identity a hit names
the genus actually present. Each genus's share is weighted by contig
length × coverage, a proxy for its share of the reads.
:::

The calls, and what each one means for the sample:

| call | evidence | what to do |
|---|---|---|
| `WRONG_TICK` | curated genus < `r 100 * params$mito$audit$rrna_minor`% of both nuclear rRNA and mitochondrial hits | tube swap, mislabel or misidentification: remove, or re-identify |
| `MIXED_SAMPLE` | two genera both carry real nuclear-rRNA share | which tick is "the sample" cannot be decided: remove |
| `CONTAMINANT_MITOGENOME` | nuclear rRNA ≥ `r 100 * params$mito$audit$rrna_major`% curated genus, mitogenome of another tick | the ID stands; drop from the mito tree; the microbiome may carry the source sample's microbes |
| `ID_SUPPORTED`, `ID_SUPPORTED_NO_MITOGENOME` | nuclear rRNA agrees with the curated genus | keep |
| `UNTESTABLE_GENUS` | the curated genus has no nuclear rRNA in nt | cannot be tested this way |
| `UNRESOLVED` | no raw BLAST file, or no tick rRNA hit | cannot be tested |

**What the audit of the previous run found, and what was done.** In the
previous run (`results/_pre_exclusion_20261008/`), step 26c called
`r if (!is.null(aud_pre)) sum(aud_pre$call == "WRONG_TICK") else "?"` samples
`WRONG_TICK`, `r if (!is.null(aud_pre)) sum(aud_pre$call == "MIXED_SAMPLE") else "?"`
`MIXED_SAMPLE` and `r if (!is.null(aud_pre)) sum(aud_pre$call == "CONTAMINANT_MITOGENOME") else "?"`
`CONTAMINANT_MITOGENOME`. On review, the clearest of these were removed and
the rest re-identified from the sequence evidence (@sec-audit,
@sec-metadata). The evidence that decided them:

* **Same-lane identity points at a source.** A foreign mitogenome 0.00% from
  another sample on the same lane implicates that sample. `8187-F1-Afimb`
  carried `6700-10-CT-Hbanc`'s *Haemaphysalis* mitogenome, at 7× coverage
  against that sample's 102×. That is consistent with carry-over into a
  low-input library. `8184-F1-N1-3-Alimb` was identical to `8302-Argusrobertsi`,
  but at twice its coverage and with 97% *Argas* nuclear rRNA, so the tube held
  an *Argas*, not a trace of one.
* **`8225-3L1`** was three pooled larvae from a long-nosed bandicoot at PHRF,
  the same host species and site as `8278-F1-Itasm`, whose *Ixodes* mitogenome
  it carried exactly. Its *Rickettsiella* gltA was also identical to the
  *I. tasmani* ticks'. It was most likely a genuinely mixed pool.
* **In every mixture where the curated genus was also present, the foreign
  mitogenome had the higher coverage**, so the coverage tie-break could not
  rescue those samples. It did rescue `8164-M1-Amorelia`: its 10× *Amblyomma*
  mitogenome had lost to a 5× *Bothriocroton* one on bitscore alone.

```{r}
#| label: aud-now
#| echo: false
aud_left <- if (!is.null(aud)) aud[call %in% c("WRONG_TICK", "MIXED_SAMPLE", "UNRESOLVED", "CONTAMINANT_MITOGENOME")] else data.table()
```

**What the audit still flags in this run.** After the exclusions and ID
corrections, no sample is called `WRONG_TICK` or `CONTAMINANT_MITOGENOME`.
`r nrow(aud_left)` sample(s) remain flagged:
`r if (nrow(aud_left)) paste(sprintf("\x60%s\x60 (%s, %s)", aud_left$sample_id, aud_left$tick_species, aud_left$call), collapse = "; ") else "none"`.
The `MIXED_SAMPLE` calls come from minority nuclear-rRNA signal from a second
genus (20–47%). In each of them the selected mitogenome matches the curated
genus, so they stay in the tree. 26c marks them
`exclude_from_species_analyses = yes`, but they were **not** removed. This
is left as a decision for review (@sec-next). The `UNRESOLVED` sample has no
≥95% tick rRNA hit. Its mitogenome sits on a long, isolated branch, so it
cannot be checked.

```{r}
#| label: sens
#| echo: false
sens <- perm[test == "tick genus, excl. mito-discordant"]
full <- perm[test == "tick genus"]
```

**The analyses in @sec-tickgroups use the corrected identifications, without
the removed samples.** As a sensitivity test, step 10b repeats the genus
PERMANOVA without the `r nrow(gd)` ticks that are still genus-discordant in
this tree. Bray–Curtis R² changes from
`r round(full[distance == "bray"]$R2, 3)` to
`r round(sens[distance == "bray"]$R2, 3)`; Aitchison from
`r round(full[distance == "aitchison"]$R2, 3)` to
`r round(sens[distance == "aitchison"]$R2, 3)`. The genus-level conclusions
therefore do not depend on the remaining discordant ticks.

### Every sample's nearest named reference

```{r}
#| label: mito-nearest-ref
#| code-summary: "Nearest reference mitogenome per sample"
tbl(mv[order(tick_genus, tick_species), .(sample_id, tick_species, verdict, nearest_ref_species,
                                           nearest_ref_dist, ref_genus_agrees, n_genes)],
    "Nearest published reference mitogenome to each sample (patristic distance, substitutions/site)")
```

Most Australian species in this collection have **no published mitogenome**,
so the nearest reference is often a congener, not the species itself. Read
`nearest_ref_dist` as "how far": below ~0.02 the sample is close to that very
species; ~0.1–0.3 is a congener; above ~1 the tip is on a long branch and its
nearest reference means little.

```{r}
#| label: mito-mono
#| code-summary: "Monophyly of curated genera and species"
tbl(rtsv("results", "mito", "tables", "mito_species_monophyly.tsv"),
    "Is each curated genus / species monophyletic in the mitogenome tree?")
```

```{r}
#| out-width: 100%
if (file.exists(R("results", "mito", "figures", "mito_tree_curated.png")))
```

# Decision log {#sec-decisions}

Every judgement call in the pipeline, where it lives, and why.

```{r}
#| label: decision-log
#| code-summary: "The decision log"
dl <- data.table::fread(text = '
area|decision|why|where
Abundance unit|TPM renormalised within the microbial fraction|most of each library has no BLAST hit; microbial share is not estimable|04_build_matrices.py
Abundance unit|Read counts gate presence, never measure abundance|TPM lets a short contig with few reads outrank a genome|config taxon_filter; 10_export_targets.py
Contig filter|>=300 bp, >=10 reads, bitscore >=100, before renormalising|short noisy contigs otherwise set the TPM denominator; effect shown in 04b|config contig_filter
Contamination|Reagent contaminants annotated, never removed|no blanks to justify removal; removal left to the analyst|03_build_taxonomy.py
Contamination|decontam frequency method only if DNA concentrations exist|the one test valid without blanks|08_composition.R
Taxonomy|Local April 2026 taxdump kept; only merged.dmp updated|keeps backfilled samples comparable with the first 120|make_merged_filtered.py
Taxonomy|Filter to microbial scope before deduplicating labels|cross-kingdom homonyms (Bacillus, Planococcus)|07_build_tse.R
Compute|Streaming LCA|original loaded 150 GB BLAST tables into RAM|lca_stream.py
Metadata|Curated CSV is the source of truth; 05b fixes formatting only, flags content|never silently rewrite field records|05b_import_metadata.py
Metadata|Sequencing submission / flowcell / lane kept as covariates|only handle on technical variation without controls|05_make_metadata_template.py; 09_diversity.R
Statistics|Two distances: Bray-Curtis and Aitchison|dominance-driven vs compositional; agreement means the result does not hinge on the choice|09, 10b
Statistics|Groups with n < 3 drawn, never tested|a mean of one tick is an individual|config tick_groups.min_samples_per_group
Statistics|PERMDISP reported beside every PERMANOVA|PERMANOVA also responds to spread|10b
Statistics|Host type tested within tick genus (blocked permutations) + marginal model|host and tick genus are confounded|10b
Statistics|Species tested after genus, permutations within genus|asks whether species matters beyond genus|10b
Statistics|Co-occurrence also stratified by tick genus (Mantel-Haenszel)|shared genus preference is not an association|10b
Statistics|BH correction within each family of tests|many endosymbiont x grouping tests|10b
Keystone taxa|Defined as dominant inherited symbionts, not network hubs|networks unreliable at this n with compositional data|10b
Figures|Heatmaps instead of 20-colour stacks; fixed colour per tick genus; second encoding everywhere|colour identity fails beyond ~8 hues and under CVD|10b, 10c, common.R
Maps|All samples with coordinates mapped, analysed or not|the map is of the sampling|10c
Maps|Co-located ticks fanned out in the interactive map only; popup gives true coordinates|identical coordinates would hide ticks|10c
Markers|All target contigs searched, not only confident calls|a marker gene is itself evidence|11-16
Markers|Competitive paralogue resolution; frames from sequence; stops flagged not fixed|Sca-family cross-hits; merged HSPs off-frame|13, 14
Markers|Viral probes from the viruses present (Jingmen-like etc.)|type-species probes found nothing|11
Trees|References chosen for breadth (cap per organism); every reference re-blasted|topology needs species, not 40 copies of one|17, 18
Trees|Figures labelled from curated metadata|tip names frozen at step 12|19b
Mito|tblastn order-wide, E-value gated, invertebrate mito code|hard/soft ticks too divergent for blastn; TGA = Trp|21, 22
Mito|No cross-gene paralogue resolution|deleted correct ND1 calls in 87/149 samples|21
Mito|Samples with < 3 genes excluded from the tree|mostly missing data -> rogue taxa|config mito.tree.min_genes_for_tree
Mito|Curated IDs cross-checked against the tree|independent molecular test of the metadata|26b
Mito|97 published mitogenomes aligned and treed with the samples|named species around every tip; enables rooting|20b; metadata/mito_ref_genomes.tsv
Mito|Every reference checked against its GenBank title before use|the supplied list contained a frog (NC_028521)|20b
Mito|References annotated by the same homology method as samples, not GenBank features|UNVERIFIED records lack features; identical gene edges for refs and samples|20b
Mito|Tree rooted on Argasidae references only; Nuttalliella left free|deepest well-established split; mislabelled samples cannot move the root|config mito.tree.outgroup_family
Environment|Maps/report in a separate env; analysis env left pinned at R 4.3|adding sf upgraded the whole analysis env|env/tick_report.yml
Mito|Candidate contig must have a tick (Ixodida) nt-BLAST LCA; no-hit contigs allowed but ranked lower|blood-meal and bacterial contigs were selected for 7 samples|21; config mito.candidates.lca_filter
Mito|Gene-count ties broken by coverage before bitscore|in a mixed tube bitscore picks the tick closest to the probes, coverage the tick with most DNA|21
Mito|Discordant samples audited by nuclear-rRNA genus at >= 95% identity|raw per-genus hit shares reflect which tick genomes are in nt, not the tick|26c; config mito.audit
Samples|Samples removed by decision listed in one file, applied at step 00 and step 21|wrong tick, mixed tube or contaminant mitogenome (26c); raw data untouched|metadata/excluded_samples.tsv
Figures|theme_classic + light-grey major gridlines on every figure|one consistent style|common.R theme_tick()
Figures|CSIRO colours, chosen and ordered by simulated colour-vision deficiency; <= 9 hues per figure; outlines + second encoding|brand palette is not CVD-safe by default; some hues too light/dark|common.R; CSIRO_colours.R
', sep = "|")
tbl(dl, page = 40)
```
